## Discussion

The study allows to facilitate the descriptive analysis and forecasting of key parameters using AI models useful for the prediction and forecast of the dynamics of the pandemic. The development of the models has enabled thanks to the availability of a large quantity of medical data from official public health sources. According to the objectives set by the study, the development of the LP platform relies on the continuous analysis of the data for the generation of alarms as a result of near real-time analyses and regular and automated data acquisition.

In the early stages of the pandemic, the use of AI to build epidemic models faced particular caution due to the lack of sufficient data and the excessive presence of noise and outliers in relation to big data collection from unreliable sources.58 Nevertheless, a lot of efforts have been made since, to enable access to data from official health authorities’ digital platforms, facilitating collection and automation of processes related to epidemic data modelling, and providing more reliable data. In this context, the proliferation of official open-access data created a thriving landscape for the use of AI in epidemic modelling and its use in the framework of DSSs.

Today, the availability of COVID-19 surveillance data in terms of daily and cumulative numbers of cases, deaths, and recoveries is no longer an issue and traditional mathematical models such as the SIR, SEIR and Stochastic models describing the dynamics of the epidemic were used in several research and were demonstrated to provide good forecasts. Predicted numbers of infected individuals using the standard SIR method against effective numbers for several countries were reported with relatively small errors ranging from 1.1% (USA, France) to 3.9% (Spain).59 An Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) modelling was used instead to project the prevalence of COVID-19 patterns in East Africa Countries. The author found relatively small forecast errors yielding mean absolute percentage errors of less than 4%.60 The key parameters predicted by the AI models in the present study represent a broad set of items chosen to provide a comprehensive picture of the COVID-19 emergency in terms of supply and demand, not only at the Italian national level but also at the regional level. This research provides an additional feature with respect to previous research which was modelling aspects of the epidemic and did not include other factors which could play a hidden role in the evolution of the pandemic.61 On the other hand, Increasing the information level using the traditional models requires major modelling development. It entails greater complexity in the systemic implementation in a real-life scenario such as the case of the ECO4CO platform. In this optics, AI offers some flexibility and adaptability to developing situations. It allows us to perform predictions with limited effective knowledge of the mathematical equations driving the pandemic dynamics, particularly in the emergence of new variants.

In general, the present study's findings have shown good predictive values for the parameters of interest. However, with regard to the regional risk classification colour code, it was observed that the performances dropped for a few regions with lower population density such as Sardinia, while the model performed well globally and in most regions of Italy (80%). Additional work can be performed to improve and derive models according to the population density. Moreover, accounting for restrictive measures such as blocking, quarantine, and travel restrictions could improve the accuracy of the prediction. In addition, vaccination data could be incorporated into forecast models, significantly improving forecast performance. Accordingly, a line of future research could be to extend the proposed prediction models with exogenous variables such as those on vaccination and restrictions.61

Regarding attendance in the emergency rooms, it was observed that it was difficult to assess the trends for small structures with greater accuracy. However, it was found that the impact of these structures is minimal in the admittance of patients at the regional level according to demographics. While the inherent impact of the predictions for these small structures may have important relative variations; in terms of absolute values, these variations are in the order of few patients and can be acceptable if adequate contingencies are taken.

The present research represents a fraction of the proposed DSS for the management of the COVID-19 response, as it covers the medical logistic aspect of the platform. The ECO4CO platform, as a whole, offers the possibility to obtain information on people's mobility and sentiment analysis thanks to systematic data collection from several sources, which entails the generation of specific alarms when thresholds are crossed.

The success of the application and similar systems is bound to several factors, which are linked to technical and human aspects such as the availability of a large quantity of official medical data from online platforms and in formats and frequencies that facilitates periodic acquisition and processing; the use of technological paradigms and development practises that allow easy integration of online services, updates and scalability and also the use of powerful and dedicated libraries for Machine Learning. Even if individual privacy is guaranteed, failure to adequately address the reuse of personal data and the digital divide problem will lead to digital epidemiology tools that undermine equity, fairness, and public trust. In contrast, a broader ethical and data governance approach, and meaningful public engagement will encourage adopting these technologies and using personal data for public health research, thereby increasing their power to address epidemics.62

On the other hand, a good synergy has been put in place between participants from different disciplines such as engineers and medical doctors. In fact, it has been argued that the lack of interdisciplinary cooperation was one of the weaknesses of research in this area. AI techniques for COVID-19 diagnosis and prediction require the integration of several different disciplines, such as computer science, medical imaging, and physicians in general. Cooperation among researchers from different disciplines is key to combining and integrating various knowledge to be more impactful in the fight against COVID-19.61

During the COVID-19 pandemic, numerous websites and web applications have been created to offer free access to COVID-19 data from a variety of sources, but more work remains to be done in order to fully enable an efficient response system in real-time and near-real-time.23 The present DSS system allows to tackle such limitation not only by providing the analyses and predictions as tools to enable decision making, but also by contributing to the creation of extensive DBs inclusive of a wider set of key parameters and factors that play a role in the understanding of the evolution of the pandemic. The versatility of the platform and the design paradigms used to allow extension of services and scalability offer possibilities for extending this application to possible health emergencies that may arise in the future. New research directions can be taken from this study by providing more extensive prediction models and incorporating additional information related to socio-economical and cultural factors. In addition, new research on the application of AI can be more pertinent in developing the logics for decision-making and providing suggestions to the health authorities.

## Conclusions

The ECO4CO DSS was developed to enable near-real-time analyses of the COVID-19 disease's epidemiological spread and trends concerning geographic distribution (from the national level to district detail). Its development involved a multidisciplinary collaboration between clinical, geographical and engineering teams and scientists with a broad range of specialisations.

The study focused on the LP sub-service, which was designed to allow the clinical and medical-related decision-making personnel to monitor, manage, and predict medical equipment logistic needs and help the scheduling of supplies for medical centres across the country, according to newly identified potential clusters.

The sub-service relies on identifying warnings related to the regional risk classification colour code, the access to the Lazio region's emergency rooms, and forecast of medical stock needs at the regional level.

The prediction of these features was made using Machine Learning algorithms and an evaluation of their outputs was performed during a pilot phase where several metrics were applied according to the type of prediction problem (e.g., time series forecast and classification).

The results obtained demonstrate that the regional risk classification colour code, based on the forecast of the number of new positives, non-critical hospitalised patients and ICU patients, show globally high scores, except for one region, which was affected by the presence of several false positives.

The prediction of the emergency room utilisation for the Lazio region yielded a very low RMSE, which shows the model's efficiency, especially for the major hospitals of the Lazio region, which admit about 90% of the region's patients.

The prediction of the medicinal consumption for the regions of Lazio and Piemonte has yielded a low RMSPE of 16%.

In the context of the pilot phase, the ECO4CO's LP subservice has demonstrated an operational capability in providing useful tools for decision support activities in the case of the COVID-19 pandemic. The diversity and extent of open-access data from the official sources provide an opportunity for continuously improving the models and providing new services for the clinical and decision-making personnel in the management of the pandemic state, while enhancing the readiness level to tackle epidemiological emergencies that may arise in the future.

The development of DSS systems enabling accurate forecasting of the evolution of new cases and drug utilisation will enable the resulting excess demand throughout the supply chain to be managed more effectively. The progression of COVID-19 across countries has shown how it has led to fundamental changes in the need for care and citizens’ behaviours more generally. Such changes put supply chains under strain. Therefore, forecasting during a pandemic becomes essential for effective government decision-making, managing supply chain resources, and for informing tough policy decisions such as, for example, imposing a lockdown. However, successful analysis and forecasting depend crucially on the availability of rich, real-time data sources.

Who is Mahmood, the charismatic artist? How did he rise to international fame in 2019? What is known about his private life? Discover 20 facts about Italian singer Mahmood.

Mahmood, whose real name is Alessandro Mahmoud, was born on 12 September 1992 and grew up in a district on the outskirts of Milan.

His Egyptian father abandoned Alessandro and his mother when the boy was five years old.

Mahmood mentions his father in at least four songs, especially in his smash hit _Soldi_. In an interview with the Italian newspaper _Il Corriere della sera_, the artist said: “The Arab sentence _waladi habibi ta’aleena_ in the song _Soldi_ refers to my father, he used to say it when we had to leave the children’s playground at Gratosoglio to go home. It means: Come on son, my love.”

Mahmood is very attached to his mother Anna, who’s originally from Sardinia. She raised her son alone. She was his mother and his father.

![Image 3](https://sp-ao.shortpixel.ai/client/to_webp,q_glossy,ret_img,w_1024,h_1022/https://vertigomag.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/BLANCO-MAHMOOD-by-Bogdan-Chilldays-Plakov-1024x1022.jpg)[](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/bookmarklet/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvertigomag.co.uk%2Fmusic%2Fwho-is-italian-singer-mahmood&media=https%3A%2F%2Fsp-ao.shortpixel.ai%2Fclient%2Fto_webp%2Cq_glossy%2Cret_img%2Cw_1024%2Ch_1022%2Fhttps%3A%2F%2Fvertigomag.co.uk%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2022%2F02%2FBLANCO-MAHMOOD-by-Bogdan-Chilldays-Plakov-1024x1022.jpg&is_video=false)
Mahmood started taking music lessons as a child. As a teenager, he took singing classes with Italian baritone Gianluca Valenti.

Mahmood auditioned for the TV talent show X Factor Italia in 2012, made the cut, but was eliminated the night of the third show.

Before rising to fame, Mahmood worked several years as a bartender in Milan.

Even though he had obtained a baccalaureate in languages, he wasn’t interested in going to university.

In 2016, he performed [Dimentica](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M6P1sb0Bn7c) in the newcomer category of the Sanremo Festival, Italy’s most important song contest.

![Image 4](https://sp-ao.shortpixel.ai/client/to_webp,q_glossy,ret_img,w_1024,h_985/https://vertigomag.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Mahmood-Blanco-by-Bogdan-Chilldays-Plakov-1024x985.jpg)[](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/bookmarklet/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvertigomag.co.uk%2Fmusic%2Fwho-is-italian-singer-mahmood&media=https%3A%2F%2Fsp-ao.shortpixel.ai%2Fclient%2Fto_webp%2Cq_glossy%2Cret_img%2Cw_1024%2Ch_985%2Fhttps%3A%2F%2Fvertigomag.co.uk%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2022%2F02%2FMahmood-Blanco-by-Bogdan-Chilldays-Plakov-1024x985.jpg&is_video=false)
Three years later, in January 2019, Mahmood won the Sanremo Festival with _Soldi_.

In May 2019, the singer rose to international fame when he performed [Soldi](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=22lISUXgSUw) at the Eurovision Song Contest in Tel Aviv. He placed second and started a successful concert tour through Europe.

_Soldi_ by Mahmood is the second most streamed Eurovision song of all time on Spotify.

![Image 5](https://sp-ao.shortpixel.ai/client/to_webp,q_glossy,ret_img,w_1024,h_937/https://vertigomag.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Sanremo-Mahmood-Blanco-1024x937.jpg)[](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/bookmarklet/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvertigomag.co.uk%2Fmusic%2Fwho-is-italian-singer-mahmood&media=https%3A%2F%2Fsp-ao.shortpixel.ai%2Fclient%2Fto_webp%2Cq_glossy%2Cret_img%2Cw_1024%2Ch_937%2Fhttps%3A%2F%2Fvertigomag.co.uk%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2022%2F02%2FSanremo-Mahmood-Blanco-1024x937.jpg&is_video=false)
Mahmood was inspired by hip-hop, rap as well as ryhtm and blues. The Fugees, Lauryn Hill, Frank Ocean, Jazmine Sullivan, Stevie Wonder and Ray Charles are some of this favourite musical artists.

Mahmood is not only a singer, but also a songwriter. He wrote most of his songs and also songs for a few Italian artists like Elodie ([Nero Bali](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iCrecXzF4CU), Andromeda), Marco Mengoni (Hola – I Say) and Michele Bravi (Presi male).

_Brividi_, which already topped the charts in Italy, will be Italy’s competing song at the Eurovision Song Contest in May 2022 in Turin. Expectations are high for the performance of Mahmood and Blanco at the ESC, especially after the international success of Maneskin.

![Image 6](https://sp-ao.shortpixel.ai/client/to_webp,q_glossy,ret_img,w_1024,h_976/https://vertigomag.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Blanco-Mahmood-Brividi-Sanremo-1024x976.jpg)[](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/bookmarklet/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvertigomag.co.uk%2Fmusic%2Fwho-is-italian-singer-mahmood&media=https%3A%2F%2Fsp-ao.shortpixel.ai%2Fclient%2Fto_webp%2Cq_glossy%2Cret_img%2Cw_1024%2Ch_976%2Fhttps%3A%2F%2Fvertigomag.co.uk%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2022%2F02%2FBlanco-Mahmood-Brividi-Sanremo-1024x976.jpg&is_video=false)
Mahmood is very interested in fashion. In the last few years, he attended several fashion shows in Paris (Valentino), London (Burberry) and Milan (Prada).

In 2019, Mahmood posed for Burberry’s Christmas campaign ([photos](https://www.vogue.co.uk/news/article/burberry-christmas-campaign-2019)).

He always wears an earring on his left ear.

![Image 7](https://sp-ao.shortpixel.ai/client/to_webp,q_glossy,ret_img,w_1024,h_991/https://vertigomag.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Mahmood-Blanco-Eurovision-1024x991.jpg)[](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/bookmarklet/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fvertigomag.co.uk%2Fmusic%2Fwho-is-italian-singer-mahmood&media=https%3A%2F%2Fsp-ao.shortpixel.ai%2Fclient%2Fto_webp%2Cq_glossy%2Cret_img%2Cw_1024%2Ch_991%2Fhttps%3A%2F%2Fvertigomag.co.uk%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2022%2F02%2FMahmood-Blanco-Eurovision-1024x991.jpg&is_video=false)
The artist used to live in a luxurious apartment of the Torre del Moro skyscraper in Milan. He said that it was his dream flat. On 29 August 2021, the 20-storey building was completely destroyed by the flames.

Mahmood is a very corteous and reserved person. He keeps his private life largely private and never speaks about his relationships.

He speaks Spanish and English fluently.

Mahmood has 1,7 million followers on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/mahmood/?hl=de) (on 6 February he had 1,5 million).

Unfortunately, Mahmood doesn’t have a press agent, which makes it nearly impossible to get an interview. Our international magazine requested several times extremely difficult for international magazines to get an interview or a photoshoot with him. The only possibility is to contact his music label Universal Music.

# Artist Profile: Baby K

by [msufjo](https://italiancultureoggi.com/author/msufjo/)Posted onJuly 18, 2020 July 19, 2020

If you can imagine [Iggy Azalea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iggy_Azalea) as an Italian rapper, then you’ve got something approaching the career of Claudia Judith Nahum, better known as Baby K. It’s not a perfect comparison, but there are some similarities early in their careers to highlight. They both spent their formative years outside of the country where they reached their greatest heights, and they both had to fight against naysayers who thought that they weren’t really hip hop or that they were getting by on their looks instead of their talent as an artist. Finally, they both broke through with [mega hits](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O-zpOMYRi0w) featuring catchy hooks sung by a featured artist. The comparisons stop there, however.

Baby K was [born in Singapore to Italian parents](https://hotmc.com/speciale-fly-girls-intervista-a-baby-k/) who then moved to Jakarta and finally to London when she was a child. While in the British capital, she honed her talent at the [Harrow School of Young Musicians](https://hym.org.uk/). At the age of seventeen she [moved to Rome](https://www.vanityfair.it/show/musica/15/09/10/baby-k-roma-bangkok-album-kiss-kiss-bang-bang) and joined the Italian hip hop scene, deciding to write and rap in Italian rather than English. After a decade of hosting radio shows and featuring on underground records, she started to gain traction with the release of her first two E.P.’s, _[S.O.S.](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.O.S.\_(Baby\_K))_, and 2011’s _[Femmina Alfa](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femmina\_Alfa)_. The latter’s title track was Baby K’s first commercially successful solo single. Embedded below, you can hear the harder sound that was much closer to conventional rap than what we’re used to from her nowadays, but the fast tempo and flow, staples of Baby K’s career, are already visible.

[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SY0K25oBExg)

The success of her second LP led to opportunities to take the next step in her career. Her [third E.P.](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lezioni_di_volo_(EP)) featured collaborations with [Ntò](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nt%C3%B2) and [Gemitaiz](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemitaiz). She opened for well-established Italian rappers like [Gué Pequeno](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gu%C3%A9_Pequeno) and [Marracash](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marracash), as well as worldwide stars like Nicki Minaj and Azaelia Banks on their dates in Italy. In 2013 she was signed by Sony and released her first commercially successful album, _[Una Seria](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Una\_seria)_, featuring the singles “[Sparami](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qCAZPp5dhSI)“, “[Killer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G9B3USSX32I)“, and “[Non cambierò mai](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PKSOiNzXs5o)” with Marracash. Although Killer was the bigger hit featuring singer and producer [Tiziano Ferro](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiziano_Ferro), the fourth and final single from the album, “[Sei Sola](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_bR-PXa9sEA)” stands out for me because of its 90s R&B vibe.

[Video 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_bR-PXa9sEA)

It was her second Sony album, _[Kiss Kiss Bang Bang](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0155P2G74/)_, that launched Baby K to heights never before reached by an Italian artist. The hands of producers [Takagi & Ketra](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takagi_%26_Ketra) are all over the disc, with forays into electropop (“[Anna Wintour](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0ra4PFEsN2k)“, “[Chiudo gli occhi e salto](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7CclS38Olq8)“) and straightforward pop music (“[Venerdì](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mfE-xrP1Pkw)“) completely dropping the pretense of hip hop. The standout song from the album was “Roma – Bangkok”, featuring Italian X-Factor alum [Giusy Ferreri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giusy_Ferreri) belting out the unforegettable hook. Although the lyrics were written by [Federica Abbate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federica_Abbate) (with a [possible assist from Rocco Hunt](https://www.olbia.it/intervista-rocco-hunt-olbia-16-11-2015/)), they are personal to Baby K, as they reference several of the places she lived (Southeast Asia, London, Rome) while growing up. There is but a faint echo of the swagger that Baby K brought to her earlier bars, but the softer sound was a smashing success. No Italian song sold more copies in the past decade, [being certified nine times platinum](https://music.fanpage.it/roma-bangkok-di-baby-k-feat-giusy-ferreri-e-disco-di-diamante-nessuno-come-lei/). The video, reminiscent of Thelma and Louise, was the first Italian music video to ever reach 100 million views, and at 260 million as of July 2020, it is still the most viewed of all time.

[Video 3](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GCPQ6_F-xfo)

Rather than resting on her laurels, Baby K reinvented herself again with a change in hair color coinciding with her biggest style shift yet. On _[Icona](https://www.amazon.com/Icona-Baby-K/dp/B07JMSVMD7/)_, the journey away from her hip hop roots accelerated. “[Aspettavo solo te](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qVjrSPsxb-Q)” and “[Come no](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pRusg4dfGzg)” are relatively straightforward pop songs with some internatonal touches, but two other tracks represented new directions for Baby K. The first single from her _Icona_ album was the delightful Latin Pop summer hit “[Voglio Ballare Con Te](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YprBWiUAKgE)“, with Spanish singer Andres Dvicio. The foray into the world of hispanic music is also apparent on the album’s biggest track, “Da zero a cento”, which was influential in establishing Reggaeton as the dominant sound in Italian pop music (especially during the summer) over the last few years. Despite the catchiness and much copied dance move, I can’t help but lament the fact that this song’s success paved the way for an avalanche of derivative and uninspired reggaeton that has flooded the airwaves in Italy.

[Video 4](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XzuV0_cot-g)

Speaking of derivative and uninspired, Baby K spent 2019 churning out songs such as “[Playa](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n5wlmrA4hTs)” and “[Buenos Aires](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7nRo-Qr9w4A)“, in addition to featuring on [Fred De Palma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_De_Palma)‘s “[Dio benedica la reggaeton](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QYOaaRzbIOg)“, which appropriately translates as God bless Reggaeton. Its frustrating, because she has always had far more musical chops than her critics have given her credit for, and until now she hadn’t been afraid to reinvent herself by embracing different musical styles. Even when she crossed over to making pop music towards the middle of the decade, there was still something fresh to enjoy, both musically and lyrically. Since the success of _Icona_, however, she seems stuck in a musical rut. There’s no new ground being being broken, and the artist that had to struggle for credibility has now become the generic autotuned popstar that her detractors caricatured her as years ago. Her latest single, “Non mi basta più” featuring musically challenged influencer [Chiara Ferragni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiara_Ferragni) is emblematic of this trend. The focus is more on exploiting the synergy between [the queen of lifestyle blogs](https://www.forbes.com/sites/clareoconnor/2017/09/26/forbes-top-influencers-instagram-it-girl-chiara-ferragni-on-building-a-fashion-empire/#3f1fb37d3001) and the queen of Italian pop in order to sell [Pantene products](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zQ7fWM5EgIc) than it is on making the kind of satisfying music that Baby K worked so hard to create for the first decade of her career.

[Video 5](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4Rp6netehE4)

# Artist Profile: Baby K

by [msufjo](https://italiancultureoggi.com/author/msufjo/)Posted onJuly 18, 2020 July 19, 2020

If you can imagine [Iggy Azalea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iggy_Azalea) as an Italian rapper, then you’ve got something approaching the career of Claudia Judith Nahum, better known as Baby K. It’s not a perfect comparison, but there are some similarities early in their careers to highlight. They both spent their formative years outside of the country where they reached their greatest heights, and they both had to fight against naysayers who thought that they weren’t really hip hop or that they were getting by on their looks instead of their talent as an artist. Finally, they both broke through with [mega hits](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O-zpOMYRi0w) featuring catchy hooks sung by a featured artist. The comparisons stop there, however.

Baby K was [born in Singapore to Italian parents](https://hotmc.com/speciale-fly-girls-intervista-a-baby-k/) who then moved to Jakarta and finally to London when she was a child. While in the British capital, she honed her talent at the [Harrow School of Young Musicians](https://hym.org.uk/). At the age of seventeen she [moved to Rome](https://www.vanityfair.it/show/musica/15/09/10/baby-k-roma-bangkok-album-kiss-kiss-bang-bang) and joined the Italian hip hop scene, deciding to write and rap in Italian rather than English. After a decade of hosting radio shows and featuring on underground records, she started to gain traction with the release of her first two E.P.’s, _[S.O.S.](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.O.S.\_(Baby\_K))_, and 2011’s _[Femmina Alfa](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femmina\_Alfa)_. The latter’s title track was Baby K’s first commercially successful solo single. Embedded below, you can hear the harder sound that was much closer to conventional rap than what we’re used to from her nowadays, but the fast tempo and flow, staples of Baby K’s career, are already visible.

[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SY0K25oBExg)

The success of her second LP led to opportunities to take the next step in her career. Her [third E.P.](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lezioni_di_volo_(EP)) featured collaborations with [Ntò](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nt%C3%B2) and [Gemitaiz](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemitaiz). She opened for well-established Italian rappers like [Gué Pequeno](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gu%C3%A9_Pequeno) and [Marracash](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marracash), as well as worldwide stars like Nicki Minaj and Azaelia Banks on their dates in Italy. In 2013 she was signed by Sony and released her first commercially successful album, _[Una Seria](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Una\_seria)_, featuring the singles “[Sparami](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qCAZPp5dhSI)“, “[Killer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G9B3USSX32I)“, and “[Non cambierò mai](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PKSOiNzXs5o)” with Marracash. Although Killer was the bigger hit featuring singer and producer [Tiziano Ferro](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiziano_Ferro), the fourth and final single from the album, “[Sei Sola](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_bR-PXa9sEA)” stands out for me because of its 90s R&B vibe.

[Video 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_bR-PXa9sEA)

It was her second Sony album, _[Kiss Kiss Bang Bang](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0155P2G74/)_, that launched Baby K to heights never before reached by an Italian artist. The hands of producers [Takagi & Ketra](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takagi_%26_Ketra) are all over the disc, with forays into electropop (“[Anna Wintour](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0ra4PFEsN2k)“, “[Chiudo gli occhi e salto](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7CclS38Olq8)“) and straightforward pop music (“[Venerdì](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mfE-xrP1Pkw)“) completely dropping the pretense of hip hop. The standout song from the album was “Roma – Bangkok”, featuring Italian X-Factor alum [Giusy Ferreri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giusy_Ferreri) belting out the unforegettable hook. Although the lyrics were written by [Federica Abbate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federica_Abbate) (with a [possible assist from Rocco Hunt](https://www.olbia.it/intervista-rocco-hunt-olbia-16-11-2015/)), they are personal to Baby K, as they reference several of the places she lived (Southeast Asia, London, Rome) while growing up. There is but a faint echo of the swagger that Baby K brought to her earlier bars, but the softer sound was a smashing success. No Italian song sold more copies in the past decade, [being certified nine times platinum](https://music.fanpage.it/roma-bangkok-di-baby-k-feat-giusy-ferreri-e-disco-di-diamante-nessuno-come-lei/). The video, reminiscent of Thelma and Louise, was the first Italian music video to ever reach 100 million views, and at 260 million as of July 2020, it is still the most viewed of all time.

[Video 3](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GCPQ6_F-xfo)

Rather than resting on her laurels, Baby K reinvented herself again with a change in hair color coinciding with her biggest style shift yet. On _[Icona](https://www.amazon.com/Icona-Baby-K/dp/B07JMSVMD7/)_, the journey away from her hip hop roots accelerated. “[Aspettavo solo te](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qVjrSPsxb-Q)” and “[Come no](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pRusg4dfGzg)” are relatively straightforward pop songs with some internatonal touches, but two other tracks represented new directions for Baby K. The first single from her _Icona_ album was the delightful Latin Pop summer hit “[Voglio Ballare Con Te](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YprBWiUAKgE)“, with Spanish singer Andres Dvicio. The foray into the world of hispanic music is also apparent on the album’s biggest track, “Da zero a cento”, which was influential in establishing Reggaeton as the dominant sound in Italian pop music (especially during the summer) over the last few years. Despite the catchiness and much copied dance move, I can’t help but lament the fact that this song’s success paved the way for an avalanche of derivative and uninspired reggaeton that has flooded the airwaves in Italy.

[Video 4](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XzuV0_cot-g)

Speaking of derivative and uninspired, Baby K spent 2019 churning out songs such as “[Playa](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n5wlmrA4hTs)” and “[Buenos Aires](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7nRo-Qr9w4A)“, in addition to featuring on [Fred De Palma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_De_Palma)‘s “[Dio benedica la reggaeton](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QYOaaRzbIOg)“, which appropriately translates as God bless Reggaeton. Its frustrating, because she has always had far more musical chops than her critics have given her credit for, and until now she hadn’t been afraid to reinvent herself by embracing different musical styles. Even when she crossed over to making pop music towards the middle of the decade, there was still something fresh to enjoy, both musically and lyrically. Since the success of _Icona_, however, she seems stuck in a musical rut. There’s no new ground being being broken, and the artist that had to struggle for credibility has now become the generic autotuned popstar that her detractors caricatured her as years ago. Her latest single, “Non mi basta più” featuring musically challenged influencer [Chiara Ferragni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiara_Ferragni) is emblematic of this trend. The focus is more on exploiting the synergy between [the queen of lifestyle blogs](https://www.forbes.com/sites/clareoconnor/2017/09/26/forbes-top-influencers-instagram-it-girl-chiara-ferragni-on-building-a-fashion-empire/#3f1fb37d3001) and the queen of Italian pop in order to sell [Pantene products](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zQ7fWM5EgIc) than it is on making the kind of satisfying music that Baby K worked so hard to create for the first decade of her career.

[Video 5](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4Rp6netehE4)

Musical artist

**Elodie Di Patrizi** (born 3 May 1990), known professionally as simply **Elodie** (Italian:[[eloˈdi]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian")), is an Italian singer-songwriter and actress. She first rose to prominence as the runner-up of the [fifteenth edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amici_di_Maria_De_Filippi#Season_15_(2015%E2%80%932016) "Amici di Maria De Filippi") of the show _[Amici di Maria De Filippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amici\_di\_Maria\_De\_Filippi "Amici di Maria De Filippi")_ (2015–2016).

Since 2015, she has released five studio albums, each of which entered the top ten of the Italian albums chart, as well as numerous successful singles. She has collaborated with Italian artists such as [Emma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Marrone "Emma Marrone"), [Elisa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elisa_(Italian_singer) "Elisa (Italian singer)"), [Giorgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgia_(singer) "Giorgia (singer)"), [Roshelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roshelle "Roshelle"), [Michele Bravi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michele_Bravi "Michele Bravi"), [Guè](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gu%C3%A8 "Guè"), [Fabri Fibra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabri_Fibra "Fabri Fibra"), [Mahmood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahmood_(singer) "Mahmood (singer)"), [The Kolors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kolors "The Kolors"), [Rkomi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rkomi "Rkomi") and [Marracash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marracash "Marracash"). She has sold over four million copies in Italy, as certified by [FIMI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federazione_Industria_Musicale_Italiana "Federazione Industria Musicale Italiana"), and earned three [MTV Europe Music Award for Best Italian Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Award_for_Best_Italian_Act "MTV Europe Music Award for Best Italian Act") nomination. She has also participated at the [Sanremo Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival "Sanremo Music Festival") four times with "[Tutta colpa mia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tutta_colpa_mia_(song) "Tutta colpa mia (song)")" (2017), "[Andromeda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andromeda_(Elodie_song) "Andromeda (Elodie song)")" (2020), "[Due](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Due_(song) "Due (song)")" (2023) and "[Dimenticarsi alle 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimenticarsi_alle_7 "Dimenticarsi alle 7")" (2025).

In 2022, Elodie made her acting debut, in the leading role of the Italian [drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_film "Drama film")_[Burning Hearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning\_Hearts "Burning Hearts")_, which premiered at the [79th Venice International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/79th_Venice_International_Film_Festival "79th Venice International Film Festival"), winning a number of awards, including a [Bif&st Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bari_International_Film_Festival "Bari International Film Festival") and the [WiCa at Rome Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome_Film_Festival "Rome Film Festival"). She also performed the original song "[Proiettili (ti mangio il cuore)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proiettili_(ti_mangio_il_cuore) "Proiettili (ti mangio il cuore)")", winner of the [David di Donatello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_di_Donatello "David di Donatello") award for [Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_di_Donatello_for_Best_Original_Song "David di Donatello for Best Original Song").

Throughout her career, Elodie has also been the face of numerous fashion and beauty brands, including [Versace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Versace "Versace"), [Sephora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sephora "Sephora"), [Puma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puma_(brand) "Puma (brand)"), [Lancome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancome "Lancome"), [Levi's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levi_Strauss_&_Co. "Levi Strauss & Co."), [Calvin Klein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Klein_(company) "Calvin Klein (company)"), [Bulgari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgari "Bulgari") and [Valentino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valentino_(fashion_house) "Valentino (fashion house)"). In 2023, [Forbes Italia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes") listed Elodie amongst "the 100 successful women in Italy" of the year. Over the course of her career, she has released numerous successful singles such as "[Guaranà](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guaran%C3%A0_(song) "Guaranà (song)")", "[Bagno a mezzanotte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bagno_a_mezzanotte "Bagno a mezzanotte")", "[Tribale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribale "Tribale")" and "[OK. Elodie was born on 3 May 1990 in [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome "Rome"), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy"). She's the daughter of Roberto Di Patrizi, a street artist, and Claudia Marthe, a former model and [go-go dancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go-go_dancing "Go-go dancing"). Elodie is of [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_people "French people")-[Black Creole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creole_people "Creole people")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-2) descent from [Guadeloupe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadeloupe "Guadeloupe"). She has a younger sister, Fey Di Patrizi. In 2008, at age of 18, Elodie auditioned during the casting session of the first season of _[X Factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X\_Factor\_(Italian\_TV\_series) "X Factor (Italian TV series)")_, being subsequently eliminated during the early stages of the competition.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-:0-3)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elodie_(singer)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 2015–2017: Career beginnings with Amici di Maria De Filippi")]

Main articles: [Amici di Maria De Filippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amici_di_Maria_De_Filippi "Amici di Maria De Filippi"), [Un'altra vita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Un'altra_vita "Un'altra vita"), and [Tutta colpa mia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tutta_colpa_mia "Tutta colpa mia")

In 2015, she competed in the [fifteenth edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amici_di_Maria_De_Filippi#Season_15_(2015%E2%80%932016) "Amici di Maria De Filippi") of Italian talent competition series _[Amici di Maria De Filippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amici\_di\_Maria\_De\_Filippi "Amici di Maria De Filippi"),_ and was selected as part of the white team, coached by [Emma Marrone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Marrone "Emma Marrone") and [Elisa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elisa_(Italian_singer) "Elisa (Italian singer)"), placing second in the final, behind [Sergio Sylvestre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Sylvestre "Sergio Sylvestre").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-:1-4) Shortly after the end of the show, Elodie signed with [Universal Music Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group") and released her debut single "[Un'altra vita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Un'altra_vita_(song) "Un'altra vita (song)")". The song peaked within the Top 40 in Italy, and was certified gold.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-FIMI_singles_certifications-5) The single was followed by her debut studio album, also titled _[Un'altra vita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Un'altra\_vita\_(album) "Un'altra vita (album)")_, which peaked at number two in Italy. The record was produced by Luca Mattioni and her former _Amici'_ s coach [Emma Marrone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Marrone "Emma Marrone"). To promote the album, the song "Amore avrai" was released as the second single. The song was nominated as "Song of the Summer" at [Radio 105 Summer Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_105 "Radio 105").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-Elodie_album_peak_positions_in_Italy-6) From September to November 2016, Elodie served as an opening act during the Adesso Tour by [Emma Marrone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Marrone "Emma Marrone") and was featured in the benefit concert special _Amiche in Arena_, organized by [Loredana Bertè](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loredana_Bert%C3%A8 "Loredana Bertè") and [Fiorella Mannoia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiorella_Mannoia "Fiorella Mannoia").

In February 2017, Elodie was announced among the competitors of the [67th Sanremo Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival_2017 "Sanremo Music Festival 2017"), with the song "[Tutta colpa mia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tutta_colpa_mia_(song) "Tutta colpa mia (song)")", written by [Emma Marrone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Marrone "Emma Marrone") and Oscar Angiuli. The song placed 8th during the final rank and peaked at number 12 on the Italian Singles Chart, being certified platinum.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-:2-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-Songs_authors-8)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-FIMI_singles_certifications-5) In the same month, the singer released her second studio album, _[Tutta colpa mia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tutta\_colpa\_mia "Tutta colpa mia")_, on 17 February 2017.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-9) The album peaked at number six on [FIMI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federazione_Industria_Musicale_Italiana "Federazione Industria Musicale Italiana")'s Chart, marking her second consecutive top 10 album.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-11) In April, the singer appeared as herself in the film _Non c’è campo_, directed by [Federico Moccia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Moccia "Federico Moccia"), for which she also contributed to the soundtrack with the song "Semplice", featured on her album _Tutta colpa mia_. From May to June 2017, Elodie was featured as a special guest during the Scriverò il tuo nome Tour by [Francesco Renga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francesco_Renga "Francesco Renga"). The two artists performed their collaboration "Così diversa" from Renga's first live album _Scriverò il tuo nome Live_.

### 2018–2019: Successful singles and collaborations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elodie_(singer)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2018–2019: Successful singles and collaborations")]

In May 2018, Elodie released the single "[Nero Bali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nero_Bali "Nero Bali")", a collaboration with singer [Michele Bravi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michele_Bravi "Michele Bravi") and rapper [Guè](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gu%C3%A8 "Guè") as the lead single from her upcoming studio project.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-12) The song received widespread success, becoming the singer's first to reach the top ten of the Italian Singles Chart, at number 10.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-13) The song was promoted during the sixth edition of [Radio 105 Summer Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_105 "Radio 105"). Subsequently, it was certified double platinum.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-FIMI_singles_certifications-5) In October 2018 Elodie released the single "Rambla", featuring Italian rapper [Ghemon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghemon "Ghemon").

On 15 March 2019, Elodie collaborated with Italian pop band [The Kolors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kolors "The Kolors") for the single "[Pensare male](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensare_male "Pensare male")".[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-14) Within two weeks, it reached the top 10 of the Italian Airplay Chart and for three consecutive weeks it was the most played song on radio, the first time for both artists. The song was certified platinum in Italy.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-15)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-FIMI_singles_certifications-5) In June 2019, the collaborative single "[Margarita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margarita_(Elodie_song) "Margarita (Elodie song)")" with Italian rapper [Marracash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marracash "Marracash") was released.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-16) The song became one of the most successful songs of the summer in Italy, receiving three platinum certifications and peaking at number six on the Italian Singles Chart and number one on the Italian Airplay Chart.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-17)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-FIMI_singles_certifications-5) In September 2019, Elodie served as a member of the jury of the [Castrocaro Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castrocaro_Music_Festival "Castrocaro Music Festival"), which aired on [Rai 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rai_2 "Rai 2"), hosted by [Stefano De Martino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefano_De_Martino "Stefano De Martino") and [Belén Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bel%C3%A9n_Rodr%C3%ADguez "Belén Rodríguez"). The following month, Elodie was featured in a re-recorded version of [Myss Keta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myss_Keta "Myss Keta")'s 2015 single "Le ragazze di Porta Venezia", subtitled "The Manifesto", with vocals by La Pina, [Joan Thiele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_Thiele "Joan Thiele"), [Roshelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roshelle "Roshelle") and [Priestess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priestess_(rapper) "Priestess (rapper)"), included in the rapper's second studio album _Paprika_.

### 2020–2021: _This Is Elodie_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elodie_(singer)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2020–2021: This Is Elodie")]

Main article: [This Is Elodie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This_Is_Elodie "This Is Elodie")

In January 2020, it was announced that Elodie would compete during the [70th Sanremo Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival_2020 "Sanremo Music Festival 2020") with the song "[Andromeda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andromeda_(Elodie_song) "Andromeda (Elodie song)")", written by [Mahmood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahmood_(singer) "Mahmood (singer)") and produced by [Dardust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dario_Faini "Dario Faini"). The song debuted at number 35 after only two days on [streaming music services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_music_services "Streaming music services") and placed 7th at the end of the competition.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-18) On 7 January 2020, the singer announced her third studio album _[This Is Elodie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This\_Is\_Elodie "This Is Elodie")_, which was released on streaming music services on 31 January 2020, and on [physical edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CD "CD") on 7 February 2020 by [Island Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_Records "Island Records"). The album, described as [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") record, contained elements from [hip hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop_music "Hip hop music"), [soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music"), [funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funk "Funk") and [reggae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggae "Reggae") and collaborations with [Guè](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gu%C3%A8 "Guè"), [Marracash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marracash "Marracash"), [Ernia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernia "Ernia"), [Gemitaiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemitaiz "Gemitaiz"), [Margherita Vicario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margherita_Vicario "Margherita Vicario"), [Michele Bravi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michele_Bravi "Michele Bravi"), [Fabri Fibra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabri_Fibra "Fabri Fibra"), [Lazza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lazza "Lazza"), [Ghemon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghemon "Ghemon") and [The Kolors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kolors "The Kolors"), as well as [Madame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madame_(singer) "Madame (singer)") in the streaming edition.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-Rockol_review-19) The album debuted at number seven on the Italian Albums Chart.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-:3-20) The week following the Sanremo Festival, both the album and the competing song "Andromeda" reached the sixth position of the relative FIMI charts.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-Elodie_album_peak_positions_in_Italy2-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-Italian_singles_chart-22)

On 13 May 2020, Elodie released the single "[Guaranà](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guaran%C3%A0_(song) "Guaranà (song)")", included in the digital re-issue of _This Is Elodie_, which was certified double platinum by FIMI for sales exceeding 140,000 copies.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-23)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-FIMI_singles_certifications-5) The following month she appeared as a featured artist on [Takagi & Ketra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takagi_&_Ketra "Takagi & Ketra")'s song "[Ciclone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciclone_(song) "Ciclone (song)")", with [Gipsy Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gipsy_Kings "Gipsy Kings") and [Mariah Angeliq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariah_Angeliq "Mariah Angeliq"), which became her fourth top 10 hit on FIMI's singles chart.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-25) In October 2020, Elodie was featured on [Carl Brave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Brave "Carl Brave")'s single "Parli parli", included in the rapper's second studio album _Coraggio_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-26)

On 30 December 2020, it was announced that Elodie would co-host the second night of the [71st Sanremo Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival_2021 "Sanremo Music Festival 2021") alongside [Amadeus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amadeus_(presenter) "Amadeus (presenter)") and [Fiorello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosario_Fiorello "Rosario Fiorello"). During the event, the singer performed a medley of her greatest success remixed with worldwide hits by [Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé"), [Raffaella Carrà](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raffaella_Carr%C3%A0 "Raffaella Carrà") and [Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madonna "Madonna").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-:4-27) In January 2021, Elodie was cast on the second season of [Amazon Prime Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Prime_Video "Amazon Prime Video") reality competition show [_Celebrity Hunted Italia_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Hunted "Celebrity Hunted"),[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-:5-28) which she won, coupled with fellow musician [Myss Keta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myss_Keta "Myss Keta").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-29)

### 2021–2023: _OK. Respira_, first arena tour and acting debut

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elodie_(singer)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2021–2023: OK. Respira, first arena tour and acting debut")]

Main article: [OK. Respira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OK._Respira "OK. Respira")

In September 2021, Elodie released the song "[Vertigine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertigine "Vertigine")", as the lead single from her then upcoming fourth studio album, set for release in 2022. The song, an [electropop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electropop "Electropop") ballad, was written by [Elisa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elisa_(Italian_singer) "Elisa (Italian singer)") and peaked at number 40 on the Italian Singles Chart.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-30) On 5 October 2021, the singer appeared as a co-host during the season premiere of the twenty-fifth season of _[Le Iene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le\_Iene "Le Iene")_. On 3 December 2021, Elodie collaborated with Italian rapper [Rkomi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rkomi "Rkomi") on "[La coda del diavolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_coda_del_diavolo_(song) "La coda del diavolo (song)")", which topped the Italian singles chart and received five platinum certifications for sales exceeding 500,000 copies in Italy, marking the first number one single for Elodie.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-31)

On 3 March 2022, Elodie released "[Bagno a mezzanotte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bagno_a_mezzanotte "Bagno a mezzanotte")" as the second single from her upcoming fourth studio album, which reached number 4 on the Italian Singles Chart.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-32) All proceeds from the single were donated to [Save the Children](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Save_the_Children "Save the Children") to help refugees from the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-33) On 10 June 2022, "[Tribale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribale "Tribale")" was released as the third single from the album. The song, which reached number 13 on the Italian Singles Chart, marks the first official release in which Elodie provides songwriting credits.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-34)

In August 2022, it was announced that the singer would make her acting debut in the Italian film _[Burning Hearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning\_Hearts "Burning Hearts")_, directed by Pippo Mezzapesa. The film premiered in the [Orizzonti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orizzonti "Orizzonti") section of the [79th Venice International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/79th_Venice_International_Film_Festival "79th Venice International Film Festival") on 3 September 2022. In the film, the singer played Marilena Camporeale, a [pentita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentito "Pentito") of the Gargano Mafia, which is based on a non-fiction book by Carlo Bonini and Giuliano Foschini and inspired by the true story of Rosa Di Fiore. Elodie's performance was met with critical acclaim which earned her a [Ciak d'oro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciak_d'oro "Ciak d'oro") as "Revelation of the Year", a special award as "Best Breakthrough Performance" at [Bari International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bari_International_Film_Festival "Bari International Film Festival") and a "Women in Cinema Award" at [Rome Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome_Film_Festival "Rome Film Festival").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-35) Elodie also co-wrote and performed the original soundtrack of the film "[Proiettili (ti mangio il cuore)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proiettili_(ti_mangio_il_cuore) "Proiettili (ti mangio il cuore)")" with [Joan Thiele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_Thiele "Joan Thiele"). The song won the [David di Donatello for Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_di_Donatello_for_Best_Original_Song "David di Donatello for Best Original Song") as well as being nominated for a [Nastro d'Argento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nastro_d'Argento "Nastro d'Argento") as Best Original Song.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-36)

On 4 December 2022, it was announced that Elodie would compete during the [Sanremo Music Festival 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival_2023 "Sanremo Music Festival 2023").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-37) The song "[Due](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Due_(song) "Due (song)")" was later announced as her entry for the Sanremo Music Festival 2023.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-38) On 9 December 2022, the single "[OK. Respira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OK._Respira_(song) "OK. Respira (song)")" was released ahead of her upcoming [album of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OK._Respira "OK. Respira"), which was released on 10 February 2023.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-39) The album marked the singer's artistic development, combining [club-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club-pop "Club-pop"), [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B") and [electronic music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-41)_OK. Respira_ peaked at number four of the Italian Albums Chart and became the first project by a female Italian artist to be certified platinum in 2023 by FIMI.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-42) On 12 May 2023 Elodie performed at her first headlining arena show at [Mediolanium Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forum_di_Milano "Forum di Milano") in [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan"), which anticipated her first arena tour, called Elodie Show 2023, starting the following November.

On 26 May 2023, Elodie released "[Pazza musica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pazza_musica "Pazza musica")", a collaboration with [Marco Mengoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Mengoni "Marco Mengoni"), which was included as a bonus track on _OK. Respira_ and as well as released as the second single from Mengoni's eighth studio album _[Materia (Prisma)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Materia\_(Prisma) "Materia (Prisma)")_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-43) On 22 September 2023, she released the song "[A fari spenti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_fari_spenti "A fari spenti")" as the lead single from the [mixtape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixtape "Mixtape")_Red Light_.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-44) The project was released as a surprise album without prior announcement. Its cover was drawn by [Milo Manara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milo_Manara "Milo Manara"). The record marked a departure from the singer's previous R&B and urban-influenced releases in favour of [house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_music "House music"), [EDM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music") and [techno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Techno "Techno") influences.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-46) The proceeds were donated to the RED association, created by [Bono](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bono "Bono") to fund health programs for women in [Sub-Saharan Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sub-Saharan_Africa "Sub-Saharan Africa").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-47) In November 2023, Elodie collaborated with Italian rapper [Sfera Ebbasta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sfera_Ebbasta "Sfera Ebbasta") for the song "Anche stasera", which served as the lead single from the rapper's fourth studio album _X2VR_.

### 2024–present: _Mi ami mi odi_ and first stadium show

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elodie_(singer)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2024–present: Mi ami mi odi and first stadium show")]

Main article: [Mi ami mi odi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mi_ami_mi_odi "Mi ami mi odi")

On 31 May 2024 Elodie released "[Black Nirvana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Nirvana "Black Nirvana")" as the lead single from her then upcoming fifth studio record. The song peaked at number 7 on the Italian Singles Chart and was certified platinum. During the summer, it was revealed that the singer will be featured on the new edition of the [Pirelli calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pirelli_calendar "Pirelli calendar"). In September, Elodie appeared as a featured artist in a remixed version of [Ornella Vanoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornella_Vanoni "Ornella Vanoni")'s song "Ti voglio", re-recorded with Vanoni and [Ditonellapiaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ditonellapiaga "Ditonellapiaga"), included on the album _[Diverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diverse\_(album) "Diverse (album)")_. On 8 November 2024, Elodie collaborated with Italian singer [Tiziano Ferro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiziano_Ferro "Tiziano Ferro") for the duet "[Feeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feeling_(Elodie_and_Tiziano_Ferro_song) "Feeling (Elodie and Tiziano Ferro song)")", released as the second official single from her upcoming fifth studio album.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-48)

The following month, she was announced among the competitors of the [75th Sanremo Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival_2025 "Sanremo Music Festival 2025"),[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-49) where she placed 12th with the song "[Dimenticarsi alle 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimenticarsi_alle_7 "Dimenticarsi alle 7")".[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-50) The song peaked at number 7 on the Italian Singles Chart and was certified gold. On 4 April 2025, Elodie released the song "[Mi ami mi odi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mi_ami_mi_odi_(song) "Mi ami mi odi (song)")", which anticipated her [fifth studio album by the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mi_ami_mi_odi "Mi ami mi odi"), released the following month. The record, a [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music"), [electropop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electropop "Electropop") and [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B") record, peaked at number 3 on the Italian Albums Chart and was certified platinum. To promote the record, the singer embarked her first stadium tour, called The Stadium Show, which consisted in a two-dates event at [San Siro Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Siro "San Siro") in [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan") and [Diego Armando Maradona Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stadio_Diego_Armando_Maradona "Stadio Diego Armando Maradona") in [Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples "Naples"). The two shows anticipated the following Elodie Show 2025, the second arena tour of the singer.

In the same year, Elodie was cast as Giada Costanzi in the [thriller film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller_film "Thriller film")_Gioco pericoloso_ and as Barbara in the [biographical drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biographical_film "Biographical film") film _[Fuori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuori "Fuori")_, directed by [Mario Martone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Martone "Mario Martone") and based on 1983 novel _L'università di Rebibbia_ by [Goliarda Sapienza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goliarda_Sapienza "Goliarda Sapienza"). For her role in _Fuori_, Elodie won her first [Nastro d'Argento for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nastro_d'Argento_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Nastro d'Argento for Best Supporting Actress").

In August 2025, Elodie was featured on [Irama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irama_(singer) "Irama (singer)")'s fifth studio album _[Antologia della vita e della morte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antologia\_della\_vita\_e\_della\_morte "Antologia della vita e della morte")_ on the track "[Ex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ex_(Irama_song) "Ex (Irama song)")".

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elodie_(singer)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Prior to joining _Amici di Maria De Filippi_, Elodie was engaged to DJ and producer Andrea Maggino.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-51) During her participation on the show _Amici_ she met the singer [Lele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lele_(singer) "Lele (singer)"). The two began a relationship in June 2016, which ended two years later.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-52)

In the summer of 2019, after the release of the hit "Margarita", she started a relationship with the Italian rapper [Marracash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marracash "Marracash").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-53) The couple split up in the winter of 2021.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-54)

In April 2026, Elodie revealed that she is in a relationship with Albanian dancer Françeska Nuredini.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-55)

## Music style and influences

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elodie_(singer)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Music style and influences")]

In an interview on Fanpage.it Elodie affirms "I'm a girl born in a low-income housing project, that's why rap, naked and raw, is a good representation of where I grew up, and I like that." and cites young Italian rappers beba, [Chadia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chadia%20Rodr%C3%ADguez "it:Chadia Rodríguez") and [Madame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madame_(singer) "Madame (singer)") as examples of "women of my generation who are not afraid to show this side. We are fierce."[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-77) In an interview with _Rolling Stone Italy_, Elodie speaks about her influences: [Etta James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etta_James "Etta James"), [Raf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raf_(singer) "Raf (singer)"), [Kaytranada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaytranada "Kaytranada"), [Nina Simone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nina_Simone "Nina Simone"), [Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé") and Italian singers [Giorgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgia_(singer) "Giorgia (singer)"), [Mina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mina_(Italian_singer) "Mina (Italian singer)") and [Lucio Battisti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucio_Battisti "Lucio Battisti").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-79) She also cities _Amici'_ s coaches [Emma Marrone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Marrone "Emma Marrone") and [Elisa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elisa_(Italian_singer) "Elisa (Italian singer)").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-80) Her music is inspired by [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music"), [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R&B "R&B"), [rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rap_music "Rap music"), [reggae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggae "Reggae"), and [urban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_music "Urban music") music.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-Rockol_review-19)

## Activism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elodie_(singer)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Activism")]

Elodie is an activist and supporter for the [LGBT rights in Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_rights_in_Italy "LGBT rights in Italy"), often siding against the right-wing party [Lega Nord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lega_Nord "Lega Nord"), regarding the campaign to pass the Italian [anti-homophobia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-homophobia "Anti-homophobia") law.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-82) Following a speech given by [Giorgia Meloni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgia_Meloni "Giorgia Meloni"), leader of the [national-conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_conservatism "National conservatism") party [Brothers of Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brothers_of_Italy "Brothers of Italy") (FdI), at the 2022 convention of the Spanish party [Vox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vox_(political_party) "Vox (political party)"), Elodie said when interviewed by Peter Gomez Homen: "It's not up to you, you're not God, you don't even come close. This is what disturbs me most about fascism. We can have different ideas, see life in a different way, but there is no need for all that animosity, that nastiness. ... It is easier to point and lash out at others for frustrations that do not concern the lives of others, but our way of life. It is much easier to lash out at black people, at gays."[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-83) After the [2022 Italian government crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Italian_government_crisis "2022 Italian government crisis"), Elodie took to her social media profiles to express her disappointment with the political programme of FdI.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-84)

Elodie often points out that she was [discriminated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discriminated "Discriminated") for her skin color and social status as a child, being a victim of [racism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racism_in_Italy "Racism in Italy").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-85)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-:7-87) She has also spoken out for [women's rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_rights "Women's rights"), calling herself a [feminist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminist "Feminist").[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-88)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-:7-87)

Musical artist

**Elodie Di Patrizi** (born 3 May 1990), known professionally as simply **Elodie** (Italian:[[eloˈdi]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian")), is an Italian singer-songwriter and actress. She first rose to prominence as the runner-up of the [fifteenth edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amici_di_Maria_De_Filippi#Season_15_(2015%E2%80%932016) "Amici di Maria De Filippi") of the show _[Amici di Maria De Filippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amici\_di\_Maria\_De\_Filippi "Amici di Maria De Filippi")_ (2015–2016).

Since 2015, she has released five studio albums, each of which entered the top ten of the Italian albums chart, as well as numerous successful singles. She has collaborated with Italian artists such as [Emma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Marrone "Emma Marrone"), [Elisa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elisa_(Italian_singer) "Elisa (Italian singer)"), [Giorgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giorgia_(singer) "Giorgia (singer)"), [Roshelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roshelle "Roshelle"), [Michele Bravi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michele_Bravi "Michele Bravi"), [Guè](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gu%C3%A8 "Guè"), [Fabri Fibra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabri_Fibra "Fabri Fibra"), [Mahmood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahmood_(singer) "Mahmood (singer)"), [The Kolors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kolors "The Kolors"), [Rkomi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rkomi "Rkomi") and [Marracash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marracash "Marracash"). She has sold over four million copies in Italy, as certified by [FIMI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federazione_Industria_Musicale_Italiana "Federazione Industria Musicale Italiana"), and earned three [MTV Europe Music Award for Best Italian Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Europe_Music_Award_for_Best_Italian_Act "MTV Europe Music Award for Best Italian Act") nomination. She has also participated at the [Sanremo Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo_Music_Festival "Sanremo Music Festival") four times with "[Tutta colpa mia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tutta_colpa_mia_(song) "Tutta colpa mia (song)")" (2017), "[Andromeda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andromeda_(Elodie_song) "Andromeda (Elodie song)")" (2020), "[Due](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Due_(song) "Due (song)")" (2023) and "[Dimenticarsi alle 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimenticarsi_alle_7 "Dimenticarsi alle 7")" (2025).

In 2022, Elodie made her acting debut, in the leading role of the Italian [drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_film "Drama film")_[Burning Hearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning\_Hearts "Burning Hearts")_, which premiered at the [79th Venice International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/79th_Venice_International_Film_Festival "79th Venice International Film Festival"), winning a number of awards, including a [Bif&st Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bari_International_Film_Festival "Bari International Film Festival") and the [WiCa at Rome Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome_Film_Festival "Rome Film Festival"). She also performed the original song "[Proiettili (ti mangio il cuore)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proiettili_(ti_mangio_il_cuore) "Proiettili (ti mangio il cuore)")", winner of the [David di Donatello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_di_Donatello "David di Donatello") award for [Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_di_Donatello_for_Best_Original_Song "David di Donatello for Best Original Song").

Throughout her career, Elodie has also been the face of numerous fashion and beauty brands, including [Versace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Versace "Versace"), [Sephora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sephora "Sephora"), [Puma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puma_(brand) "Puma (brand)"), [Lancome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancome "Lancome"), [Levi's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levi_Strauss_&_Co. "Levi Strauss & Co."), [Calvin Klein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Klein_(company) "Calvin Klein (company)"), [Bulgari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgari "Bulgari") and [Valentino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valentino_(fashion_house) "Valentino (fashion house)"). In 2023, [Forbes Italia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes") listed Elodie amongst "the 100 successful women in Italy" of the year. Over the course of her career, she has released numerous successful singles such as "[Guaranà](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guaran%C3%A0_(song) "Guaranà (song)")", "[Bagno a mezzanotte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bagno_a_mezzanotte "Bagno a mezzanotte")", "[Tribale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribale "Tribale")" and "[OK. Respira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OK._Respira_(song) "OK. Respira (song)")".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elodie_(singer)#cite_note-1)
